A beautiful game that is held back by shallow tedium. It might have benefited from simply being a visual novel, where it could emphasize its diverse cast of characters, wonderful art, writing and setting.

However, if you feel that your real day-today-day is spent selflessly helping others, this game will only frustrate you. Charming, gourgeously rendered art and characters will let you down by never helping you in any meaningful way. The majority of the game is spent tierlessly gathering resources for your passangers, only for the passangers to pat you on the back and tell you to get back to work. This problem is compounded when a passanger is also rude, meaning you are required to cater to the every whim of an impolite person.

I desparately wanted to enjoy this game, but it is unfortunately a customer service simulator.
if i had known gustav was my long lost art critic lover from japan i wouldn't have let him starve so often. very weak storytelling for a game that wants to make you feel something

This game gives me very mixed feelings.

On one hand, it has a gorgeous art style, an amazing soundtrack, a touching story and spirit quests, a fluid and simple movement system that makes run and jump around fun, and an interesting setting/world. These aspects, are phenomenal, there are some things that aren't fleshed out properly and spirits that are hit or miss, but it's a genuinely beautiful game.

On the other hand, it has a mining, fishing, farming, cooking and material refinement aspect that's done through a series of minigames, and is an actual chore. And worst, no option to automate these tasks or just buy the materials from a shop. All while, said materials are mandatory for main and secondary progression.

You want an specific type of wood? you will have to chop down a tree in a boring "move your analog from left to right minigame".
You want planks to build or upgrade something? put the logs in a machine and move your analog up and down to cut it in planks.
You want ores? mine for some with a "hold down and release a button" minigame.
You want to refine these ores? put them in the foundry and start a minigame to control the heat by running from left to right to control two air blowers, and if you're too fast, you will have to start from the beginning. 
You want to fish in order to feed the spirits? cast the reel and hold down a button to pull it back multiple times for multiple fishes.
You need a fruit or vegetable? plant and wait.
There is a certain minigame, where you have to run around your ship collecting materials, around six or seven of them for different types. And that's all you do, you run and jump around trying to catch whatever you need while they sometimes run from you.

This gets repetitive and boring way too quickly, since the minigames are always the exactly same, there is not much skill involved, except for the platforming ones, and they're just not fun. But you have to do all of them if you want to advance in the game's content, since there is no other option to get the materials.

It also has a whole bunch of fetch, simple and samey quests that don't reward you, really, you don't get any reward after finishing some quests, just a "thank you", even in the main game.

Not recommended because this game is not good to actually play, due to all the grind that often gets in the way of the good parts.

I want to make a positive review for this game so very very badly. Unfortunately, I can't.

I've been playing this game for a few years now on different platforms, and likely have over 100 hours on it in total. I adore it. I would seriously recommend than anyone who can play it, should give it a whirl to see if they like it. 

Buuuuut, over the past few months, a few chronic conditions of mine have severely worsened, and I've gotten a lot more sensitive to flashing lights and things in that wheelhouse. I looked in the game to see if there were any accessibility options, anything to turn off the constant flashing lights in the game. Nope. I looked online to see if anyone's asked about this. Apparently, after being asked to add accessibility features, the devs just said no. This is secondhand info and I can't find the source so take it with a grain of salt, but I'm a little miffed that there wouldn't just be an accessibility feature in-game anyways. I want to play this game that's helped me so thoroughly through hard parts of my life. I want to be able to play it pain-free! But that's just not possible, most days.

Disabled people deserve to enjoy their hobbies without fear of pain or medical flares due to something as avoidable as flashing lights and eyestrain. We deserve to enjoy our media without fear, without stress for our health. 

I'll still probably be buying the fangamer plush when I'm able to save up for it. Dude, the Atul plush is adorable!! And I'm still obsessed with the game, of course. I just. Can't play it anymore. Which breaks my heart.

Make games more accessible. We deserve to see the world just as everyone else can, and the art within it. Let me play my favorite game again.

Don't get this game. Only if it's like- 80%+ off. This game is BAD. Not good. This game is not fun, it's repetitive and boring, all the music everywhere is pretty much identical, the art of every single character looks bad for some reason and the game is genuinely annoying to play. Here is all the issues I found with it in specified segments.

Fishing:
The fishing is- Well, it's bad. It's not fun. You just hold left click when the line isn't red and when it is you release. This mechanic is completely random. Everything has the same pool of patterns and they're all boring and take roughly 50-ish seconds and you get a fish which does nothing except make a food that the NPC's you give it to won't even appreciate.

Gameplay:
The gameplay is utterly boring. It's a resource collector somehow more boring than watching paint dry. You just go around and get resources from islands which takes like one to two minutes to travel to and then you get like 14 of something and go back to your island to spend the next 15 minutes making materials so that an NPC can get a piece of furniture they'll tell you: "It looks like a dead seagull, but I guess it's fine." which makes it seem like you wasted your time. In addition if you want to make your crops grow up in less than 20 minutes- You'll need to sit there and hold R then random repeating combinations of WASD, and they're so easy that you can literally do it blind if you've seen it once. Moreover than that, it's extremely annoying to hear the same 4 notes on repeat and they're not even determined by the notes you click.

Visuals:
E V E R Y T H I N G I S C H E A P A S S E T S. Incase that was difficult to read- It said: "Everything is cheap assets." Which is what is in this game. The art genuinely looks bad. My eyes hurt from trying to watch this game normally, and there's thousands of bright lights in every single thing that basically blind you randomly for like- I don't ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ know- CREATING A SINGLE PLANK WHICH YOU WILL DO 80 TIMES. It's horrible for your eyes. The NPC's also look bad, they either look like their models are downscaled in bits and they look pixelated and ugly- Or they just move extremely slow and have a fast animation, etc.

NPCs:
The NPC's are terrible. They do practically nothing and demand your entire attention, talking to them is a chore because they yap and you have to wait for the entire text bubbles to load and then press E OF ALL THINGS, which I hope for you that you can change, because it's bad. And if you press Space any time during the interaction- You just jump and it completely resets. On top of that, all the NPC's have the same Voiceline for each of them which is extremely annoying and genuinely will hurt your ears because they spam it like 13 times each conversation. They also all have like 10 different sprites, 8 of which being for walking most likely, and the other 2 for when they're talking/finished doing something/finished talking/want something from you/anything and one for them to have a character smoke. It's not enjoyable to interact with them, none of them have any explanation for what they do, for example: Character tells you to go to an island she knows because she visited it earlier -> you rescued this character from an island she was never capable of leaving before ever. How does she know like 20 different islands to tell you to go to to get a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ lemon so she can say to you: "I actually hate lemons, but I like working you"? She just does. Every character does that stuff too btw.

Movement:
Movement in this game is bad, it's not good. If you need to jump up a platform you can't press any buttons except Holding space and then waiting for an egrigiously long climb animation, and everything has bright lights for no reason aswell. Should probably say if you have any problems such as: Epilepsy or just dislike being blinded by random bright lights- This game will quite literally kill you. So don't do that.

I really wanted to like this game. The art is amazing, music is a vibe and the world seems interesting but all of that being held back by a rather repetitive loop of gameplay that is such a slog to interact with. Everyone saying this game is about death and letting people go but none of the characters I met were interesting enough for me to shed a tear for them except only one or two. This is a work of art but not a fun game.
after a while it gets quite tedious, like a clicking simulator

Before I say anything else: PLEASE do not get this game if you have any form of light sensitivity. Epilepsy, migraines, what have you. There is flashing lights associated with SO many activities you do (getting a new spirit, bringing a spirit to the afterlife, cutting down trees, mining...) and you can't turn it off. Please stay safe!

That being said, I'm incredibly conflicted on whether to recommend this game or not. It is gorgeous, especially at the start. The art, the music, the vibes? All amazing. A lot of the earlier spirits are amazing, but once you get to late game (I'm talking [spoiler]Bruce & Mickey, Elena, Jackie & Daria[/spoiler], those spirits) it starts just getting. Annoying.

Maybe it's because I'm regretting my choice to try 100%ing this game, but the spirits get more and more unlikeable with time, and I connect with them less and less. [spoiler]I don't believe the intended effect was for me to be happy to send Bruce & Mickey to the Everdoor, but that sure is what happened. Hated their entire arc. Also the fact they bully everyone on board and free my sheep from their corrals whenever they get sad.[/spoiler]

Maybe I'll reconsider this when I'm less tired from all the time spent cooking and fishing and [spoiler]trying desperately to finish Elena's mission[/spoiler], but for now, this game gets one very sad Do Not Recommend from me. Still trying to 100% it, though, it's enjoyable in its own way 1/4 of the time.

Occasional moments of beauty and emotion interspersed across 20+ hours of the most tedious gameplay loop I have ever seen. To put it short, this game just simply drags on and when 90% of your playtime is just resource gathering so you can build sh*t to progress stages of a questline, you start to wonder whether this is really a 'game' or just something that wastes your time.

Also, don't fall for the absolute psy-op that this game will "break you" or is one of the most emotional works of media ever created - it won't, and it isn't. A lot of the 'goodbyes', which serve as the main payoff for the never-ending onslaught of tedious tasks the game subjects you to, are mainly just the characters riffing the exact same dialogue they've been peddling you for the last 5 hours without any actual character development being involved. 

But hey, 'in real life, some people really don't learn their lesson,' or something. One of the best characters in the game, and the only real one I had an inkling of an emotional connection to aside from Alice, just ups and vanishes without any explanation. But hey, 'in real life, some people just disappear or something.' Bleh.

and second by its baffling increase in labor just after 2 hours into this 'cozy' game.

While 〈Spiritfarer〉 may have some particularly good stories and narratives in its later parts, the player struggles to reach them unless its gameplay offers any pressure to immerse.
The driving forces to immerse in 〈Spiritfarer〉 are the beautifully lush artstyle and its reputation as a 'touching masterpiece'.
But at the time when the toad uncle and snake grandma ask for their houses, the player is overwhelmed by its repetitive nature which overshadows its artstyle, leading the player to doubt the game's high esteem.

Compared to 〈To The Moon〉 which shares similar flaws, the gameplay is less tedious, but the early part that lacks sufficient story context and a much larger volume than the 3 hour-long 〈To The Moon〉 induce a fatal stage of ennui during its gameplay.

I would not usually write a negative review on anything, as I am usually more inclined to let people enjoy things, but I think I ought to give my two cents here since I was very dissapointed by this game. I can see how some people would enjoy the game, but there are some big flaws that I think would make others very frustrated and disapointed by it. So, just a heads up if someone happens to run into the review.

First of all, the game is gorgeous, with very wonderful animations and character design. And the core idea of the game, I think, is very intriguing. Sadly, this is as far as my compliments go.

- THE STORY: which seems to be the focus of the game, is in my opinion very poorly told until the very end of the game, the spirits you interact with mostly seem to speak either in riddles or with a shared familiarity with Stella, the main character, that you don't have. That is, they will talk about events and people that you (the player) know nothing about, and, at least on my end, I was very confused with what their deal was, and what was the main character connection to them. As a result, the moment where you have to help the spirits "move beyond", which is meant to be a heartfelt and difficult decision, never managed to have much emotional impact to me. Some people seem to really resonate, and even cry, with these scenes and stories, so I won't deny that it definetly works for some people, but it definetly did not for me.

-THE GAMEPLAY: is the main drawback of the game, as it is INCREDIBLY tedious. You will have to farm an unreasonable amount of resources, and, more annoyingly, refine them in several stations accross your boat. Refining materials in this game takes forever, both due to the sheer amount of refining you will have to do, as well as the animations, which, again, are very pretty the first 10 times you see them, to then be maddening for the next 100 times. The forge is particularly bad in this regard. 

-TRAVEL, which is a core mechanic of the game, also takes forever. The fast travel system is very tedious. Picture this, you want to travel from point A to point B, far away on the map. What you have to do is: 1. Go to the cabin, and select the map, choose to travel to the closest fast travel location, close off the map. 2. Wait x amount of time, usually around 40 seconds to 1 minute, to make it to the fast travel location. 3. Walk to the middle of the boat, where the fast travel station is, jump off the ship, interact with the fast-travel and select the new station. 4. An 5 seconds or so animation plays. 5. You are in the new fast travel location, now, walk to the cabin, open the map, look for the island you were visiting and select it. 6. Wait another 40 seconds or so to make it to the new island.  Now, imagine doing this dozens or hundreds of times in the game, and also consider that if the boat encounters something in the way, it will stop, and if midnight arrives, the boat will also stop and force you to sleep for the night. The whole song and dance gets old quick. This slow system would work if you had to travel less across islands, but you actually have to move around the map a lot in order to complete the characters requests.

-THE BOAT: which you will spend most of your playtime in, starts off quite quaint and interesting. As you progress the story however, it will grow into an untennable collection of buildigs, stations and farms stack on top of each other and riddled with wooden stairs, pillars, and ugly "gaps" in between buildings. The buildings don't seem to have much artistic cohesion and clash against each other quite a bit, and it is hard to make it organized in a way that is both easy to navigate and use and aesthetically pleasing. 

Because of this, I would caution about playing the game, there is definetly some good stuff to enjoy in it, but overall, the experience was tedious and unsatisfying. I feel bad because there is clearly a lot of passion behind this project.
Slow start forcing interaction with uninteresting NPCs. The coop is oversold as second player has no action controls to interact with most objects, this is a non starter for me and my wife.

It's a beautiful game, and I really appreciate the themes and the emotional story moments of the game.

Unfortunately the gameplay is very tedious. It's mostly busy work that consists of running from one place to another completing repetitive small tasks and mini games. To make it worse there are short animation locks and UI transitions that get annoying after a while. There doesn't seem to be much progression either that would reduce the amount of busy work. In fact it gets worse as the number of quests and different resources increases.

There's not much actual "management" that would require complex decision making. Even though it's technically an open world game, the game loop is so limited and straightforward that it almost seems linear: You choose which request or other objective you want to complete next, then obtain the resources needed to complete it, and finally go to the place where the objective is completed. Repeat ad nauseum.

In short, it's a lot of work for not enough payoff. At some point I realized that I'd rather watch the story scenes on youtube instead of playing the game.

One is the moment to moment gameplay which is the base building resource gathering and crafting (which is incredibly slow and repetitive bordering on tedious).
Second is the story lines of the spirits and you helping them. 

The glue that holds these two elements together is the cozy, chill and wholesome atmosphere of the game, but if you don't fall in love with that vibe the game becomes incredibly tedious. Those who enjoy these elements will absolutely love this game, as you can see from all the positive reviews. So if that sounds like your cup of tea you can ignore my review. I won't go as far as to say this game is bad, its just not for me.
